problem_text:
A logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over an upcoming operational span of 18 weeks. The initial stockpile at the outset of the planning interval is 24 kiloliters. In each week t = 1, ..., 18, the vendor permits the company to request a delivery, the volume of which must be contained within the bounds of 20 and 40 kiloliters. However, any delivery request will experience a lead time of 1 week before it becomes available to meet consumption requirements or augment the stockpile.

The weekly consumption of the additive is specified as follows:
* Week 1: consumption 15 kiloliters
* Week 2: consumption 52 kiloliters
* Week 3: consumption 30 kiloliters
* Week 4: consumption 20 kiloliters
* Week 5: consumption 27 kiloliters
* Week 6: consumption 32 kiloliters
* Week 7: consumption 52 kiloliters
* Week 8: consumption 55 kiloliters
* Week 9: consumption 17 kiloliters
* Week 10: consumption 17 kiloliters
* Week 11: consumption 34 kiloliters
* Week 12: consumption 30 kiloliters
* Week 13: consumption 58 kiloliters
* Week 14: consumption 30 kiloliters
* Week 15: consumption 29 kiloliters
* Week 16: consumption 31 kiloliters
* Week 17: consumption 58 kiloliters
* Week 18: consumption 10 kiloliters

Supply deficits are tolerated, but any unsatisfied consumption is entirely forfeited and will not be carried forward. Throughout the 18-week horizon, all additive quantities may be treated as continuous measures, and the total volume of physically held stock at any moment must remain within the storage facility's capacity limit of 39 kiloliters.

Specifically, during week 8, the maximum allowable delivery quantity is restricted to 22 kiloliters. Furthermore, by the conclusion of week 17, the on-site stockpile must be maintained at a level no lower than 16 kiloliters.

The aggregate expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three distinct elements: the procurement cost, calculated at 2 monetary units per kiloliter ordered; the storage cost, levied at 3 monetary units per kiloliter of stock transferred from one week to the next; and a deficit penalty, assessed at 8 monetary units per kiloliter of unfulfilled consumption. The objective is to ascertain the optimal delivery volume for each week and to monitor the consequent stockpile and deficit levels, thereby minimizing the total expenditure.
